title: [P2.15d-i-pre-budget-1b consumer] Control Room live-lane client for the budget commitment read route, and its dev-proxy roster entry
description:
PARENT: task-80b6bf7cd73040e5bf15069d31af81a8 (the daemon-side producer). GRANDPARENT: task-be80cb74, whose block named this whole chain. Carried in `dependsOn` as a field, not just prose.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE ROW AND NOT SCOPE I DROPPED. task-80b6bf7c's first plan covered the daemon route, its wiring, the seed seam AND this control-room leg. `moe.submit_plan` refused it: `[CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION] Plan too large: 20 distinct affected files (max 10)`. The daemon slice alone is 8 files, so the control-room leg is what did not fit. Split along the SPIDR Interface axis: the parent owns the daemon-side producer and the storeless fetch seam; this row owns the browser-side consumer. Nothing was narrowed away — the clause moved to a row that names it, with the dependency as a field so the runtime enforces the order.

WHAT IT DELIVERS. A Control Room live-lane reader for the parent's `/budget/commitment/read` route, modeled on `apps/control-room/src/live/live-planning-run.ts:322` `readPlanningRun`: a module-const path, an INJECTABLE `post` defaulting to `fetch`, and an outcome mapper that carries the daemon's own refusal code and layer rather than restamping them. Plus the route's entry in `DEV_PROXY_PATHS`, without which the browser cannot reach it in development at all.

NAMED FAN-OUT CONSUMER, MEASURED AT FILING TIME, NOT LEFT FOR THE WORKER TO DISCOVER (epic rail 7B/8A). `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts:5` is a frozen literal array and `apps/control-room/src/live/live-document-proxy.test.ts` pins it THREE ways: `expect(DEV_PROXY_PATHS).toStrictEqual([...])` on the full literal at :6, uniqueness at :22, and the built proxy map's exact key order at :27. Adding one path reds all three by construction. The roster is sorted; insert in sort position or :27 reds on ordering alone.

PRECEDENT WORTH KNOWING BEFORE DISPUTING THE ROW'S EXISTENCE: `/product-contract/gate-1/read` (89533c6c, 6 hours before this filing) is NOT in `DEV_PROXY_PATHS`. A daemon read route can ship without browser reachability, so this leg is a real deliverable rather than a formality — it is the difference between a route the seed can call and a route the Control Room can call. task-be80cb74's DoD 4 names the demo lane's live journey specifically, which is why it is in scope for the chain at all.

DO NOT EDIT `budgetRef: hex64("bb")` at `apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts:218`. Replacing that literal is task-be80cb74's own DoD 4, same file, and taking it here collides on the same lines. Anchor on `git grep -n 'hex64("bb")'` rather than the coordinate: that file moved once already at 37f95c18.

The root vitest include has no `apps/**`, so `pnpm test` runs ZERO tests for every file this row touches. Evidence comes from `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and its `Test Files N passed` count line.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK FIRST, in a row comment quoting `git rev-parse HEAD`, greps unpiped with exit codes plus a positive control: (a) the parent's route path constant exists and is exported from apps/daemon/src/http/ (EXIT 0) - this is a CONSUMER-EDGE check on landed bytes, not a check that this row's own file exists; (b) `DEV_PROXY_PATHS` still does NOT contain the path; (c) live-document-proxy.test.ts still pins the roster at the three sites named in the description, with their current line numbers re-derived by grep rather than trusted. If the parent has not landed, block naming task-80b6bf7c rather than stubbing its path.

A Control Room live-lane reader posts `{runId}` to the parent's route path and returns either the commitment ref or the daemon's refusal carrying ITS OWN code and layer - never restamped into a local code. Modeled on live-planning-run.ts's shape: module-const path, injectable `post` parameter defaulting to `fetch`, pure outcome mapper split from the transport so it is testable without a network.

Arms assert the SPECIFIC code AND layer for each refusal the daemon can forward (at minimum the pre-finalization `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_UNSEALED` @ `APPROVAL_RUN_BINDING`), plus a success arm, plus a non-200 / unreadable-frame arm. An arm asserting merely that the call did not succeed is vacuous and does not satisfy this clause.

The route path is added to `DEV_PROXY_PATHS` in sort position, and all three pins in live-document-proxy.test.ts are updated in the SAME step: the `toStrictEqual` literal at ~:6, the uniqueness assertion, and the built-map key-order assertion. Quote the updated literal in the step note.

Gates standalone and unpiped with counts quoted: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` (quote the `$ tsc` echo as execution evidence) and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (quote `Test Files N passed` - exit 0 with no count line is UNVERIFIED, not a pass). A bare `pnpm test` count line is NOT admissible for any apps/** claim.

A mutation drill with a restore proof: break one field of the mapper's forwarding (e.g. drop the layer) and show a named arm reds BY NAME, then restore. New files are untracked, so `git diff` is blind to them - `git status --porcelain` the exact paths first and prove any untracked restore by SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup, in a call separate from the restore. A green drill is a finding, not a pass.
taskRails: Consumer only. This row adds no daemon-side bytes and defines no new refusal vocabulary - it forwards what the parent's route already answers.
Keep the daemon's refusal code and layer intact end to end; a browser-local code would hide which layer refused.
Do not touch `budgetRef: hex64("bb")` at live-dispatch-payloads.ts - that literal belongs to task-be80cb74 DoD 4.
Explicit-pathspec commits re-derived at commit time; foreign WIP preserved; <=250 lines per production source file.
Anchor every reference on the SYMBOL via `git grep -n` at a quoted sha, never on a line coordinate - four anchors in this epic went stale in the last 24h.

implementationPlan.description:
PHASE 3 -- TESTS FIRST, RED BEFORE ANY PRODUCTION BYTE (epic rail 3). Write every arm FAILING; quote the red count line before step 3 starts.

Most arms drive the PURE mapper directly, not the transport, because a transport-level test with a stubbed `post` cannot distinguish 'mapped the refusal correctly' from 'the stub handed back the object unchanged'.

MAPPER ARMS -- each asserts the SPECIFIC code AND the layer string (global rail 1: an arm asserting merely that the call did not succeed is vacuous and does not satisfy DoD 3):
1. SUCCESS: an exact COMMITMENT frame at status 200 yields the ref. Also assert an EXTRA-KEY frame is rejected -- the exact-key discipline the daemon route uses on the way in must not be abandoned on the way out.
2. PRE-FINALIZATION at HTTP 200: `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_UNSEALED` @ `APPROVAL_RUN_BINDING` survives with BOTH strings intact. This is DoD 3's named minimum.
3. MISSING PREREQUISITE at HTTP 200: `BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING` @ `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE`.
4. ROUTE-LOCAL refusal at HTTP 200: the capability-denied code at the route's own private layer -- proving a route-local code is forwarded identically to an upstream one.
5. LISTENER refusal at a NON-200 status (400 request-invalid, 503 unavailable): its code survives and is NOT flattened into a generic invalid. THIS IS THE ARM THAT PROVES THE ORDERING, mirroring live-planning-run.ts:278-281.
6. NON-REFUSAL NON-200 and unreadable/non-object frames: mapped to a visible error outcome, not silently to success.

TRANSPORT ARMS via an injected `post`: a resolved response is mapped; a THROWN send yields the transport-failed outcome; a body that fails `.json()` yields the invalid outcome.

DIVERGENCE (epic rail 7A): arms 2, 3 and 4 all travel the same forwarding path, so each must be an input where its own code is the ONLY one that can appear. State beside each how it differs from its siblings. Do not collapse them into one parameterised case that could pass with a single shared code.
implementationPlan.note: RED FIRST, and red for the RIGHT reason — module absence, not a mis-written assertion. `npx vitest run src/live/live-budget-commitment.test.ts` from apps/control-room: `Error: Failed to resolve import "./live-budget-commitment.js" from "src/live/live-budget-commitment.test.ts". Does the file exist?`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests no tests`. 17 arms in two describes. MAPPER ARMS (pure, no transport, because a stubbed `post` cannot distinguish "mapped correctly" from "the stub returned the object unchanged"): exact COMMITMENT frame -> ref; EXTRA-KEY COMMITMENT frame -> ERROR, so the daemon's exact-key discipline on the way IN is not abandoned on the way OUT; empty-string ref -> ERROR; the three forwarding arms each asserting BOTH strings — `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_UNSEALED @ APPROVAL_RUN_BINDING` (DoD 3's named minimum), `BOOTSTRAP_PREREQUISITE_MISSING @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE`, and the ROUTE-LOCAL `BUDGET_COMMITMENT_READ_CAPABILITY_DENIED @ BUDGET_COMMITMENT_READ` proving a local code forwards identically to an upstream one; the ORDERING arm as an it.each over both listener codes at 400 and 503, which is what proves the refusal check runs BEFORE the status gate (otherwise a non-200 refusal flattens to a generic invalid and the real code is lost); a non-refusal 500 -> ERROR never success; and an it.each over null / array / string / empty-object bodies. DIVERGENCE, written beside each arm per epic rail 7A rather than left implicit: the pre-finalization frame is reachable only from a run that EXISTS but is unsealed; the prerequisite frame's run does not exist at all so the binding check is never reached; the route-local frame is refused at the capability gate BEFORE the port is asked, so no durable state is read. One input, one constructible code each — they are not a parameterised case that could pass on a single shared code. TRANSPORT ARMS via injected `post`: the posted body is asserted to be EXACTLY `JSON.stringify({runId})`; a THROWN send -> transport-failed at this reader's own layer; a body failing `.json()` -> invalid; and a daemon refusal surviving the round trip unchanged. Plus a pin that the path constant equals the landed daemon spelling.

implementationPlan.description:
PHASES 6+7+8 -- DOCS, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, REGRESSION, COMMIT.

(a) DOCS: inline comments only where the WHY is non-obvious, at `live-planning-run.ts`'s density. Exactly one is genuinely non-obvious and MUST be written: why refusal recognition precedes the status gate. Copy the reasoning, not the words.

(b) ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW -- load the `adversarial-self-review` skill and read the diff as an attacker. Under SPEED this plan auto-approved with no independent review and the planner is the executor, so this and (c) are the ONLY adversarial pass before QA, and both QA seats have said they will grade the PLAN against the DoD rather than only the diff against the plan. Specifically: does any arm assert an outcome shape without its code AND layer? Does a non-200 refusal keep its code? Does an extra key in the response frame get rejected? Is the roster insert in sort position, and did the key-order pin actually run? Is the path constant the one verified on landed bytes in step 1, or one copied from prose? Is there a `.js` bridge that is needed but absent, or present but dead?

(c) REGRESSION -- load `regression-check`.
